teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Locate the failed stage from its execution status and retained artifact records, preserving the identities of successfully completed required stages. Catch the declared recoverable error with try/except, record the failure and apply only the supplied recovery action rather than silently declaring success. After a repair, rerun the affected required quality check and stop if it still fails; failure recovery must not bypass dataset or model gates.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Reuse a completed upstream artifact only when its recorded identity and required validation are still valid for the resumed downstream stage. In an existing Cloud Build YAML/JSON configuration, each steps item declares its execution image in name and its command in args or script; wire the function/test entry point into the assigned stage. Assign step IDs and set waitFor to the required preceding step IDs; downstream execution depends on those steps completing successfully, not just their textual location.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Keep required gate failures fatal: do not set allowFailure or add failing gate exit codes to allowExitCodes, and ensure a rejected Python gate exits unsuccessfully. Use the configured Pub/Sub artifact/event trigger with its configured payload bindings and filters to run the existing pipeline, then inspect actual stage results and resolved inputs for accepted and rejected fixtures. The recovery function must distinguish the injected recoverable exception from unrelated failures, then retry from the verified artifact boundary and inspect that the retry and later required gates actually executed.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: With the declared PyYAML dependency, import yaml; write a mapping/list configuration with yaml.safe_dump(config, file_handle), reload it with yaml.safe_load(file_handle), and inspect the required resolved fields before submitting it to the existing runtime. Safe loading accepts standard YAML tags, not arbitrary Python object constructors. Bound the recovery fixture’s partial effects to declared named Cloud Storage artifact uploads and reconcile each declared output before repeating it: use blob.exists(), blob.reload() and its generation to retrieve the existing bytes, verify their expected content hash and required validation, then skip only the matching completed upload; create a missing output with blob.upload_from_filename(path, if_generation_match=0). If the create reports 412 Precondition Failed, re-read and verify the already-created output instead of overwriting it; conflicting content or failed validation stops recovery. Inject failure after one declared output upload but before the remaining stage work; assert recovery retains the first output’s generation/hash, completes only missing uploads, runs the retried stage and downstream required gates, and reports failure for an invalid existing output. Invoke recovery again on the completed fixture and assert no extra output generations or uploads occur, while required validation is not bypassed.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content: Inject failure after declared output A is uploaded but before B. Inspect A's existence, generation, bytes, expected hash and validation. Skip that matching completed upload; create missing B with if_generation_match=0. If creation reports 412, re-read and verify the already-created output instead of overwriting it. Conflicting bytes or failed validation stop recovery. Retry from the verified boundary, run the affected stage and downstream required gates, and inspect their results. Invoke recovery again on the completed fixture and verify no extra uploads or generations while validation remains enforced. Catch only the declared recoverable exception; unrelated failures are not permission to resume.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: Recovery is not ‘ignore failure and continue.’ A completed upload is reusable only with verified identity and validation, and retry must not overwrite a conflicting artifact.

teaching_blocks.content: The active model must be traceable to its training record, code and data. Similar names across deployment and tracking records do not establish this lineage; inspect the supplied identity links pair by pair.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Resolve the deployed registry version, artifact source and originating run. Compare that run's dataset, configuration and artifact identities with the deployment and approval record. Download the exact recorded artifact generation and verify its content identity. Inspect the referenced local commit with git rev-parse and git show to confirm that the commit exists, rather than copying a revision string into the audit. In a failure fixture, a deployment linked to artifact B while approval covers A must be flagged. Preserve missing links and mismatches explicitly. The audit connects evidence that exists; it should not infer an unrecorded training source from a familiar model name.

Walk the identity chain in order, comparing deployment to registry, registry to artifact/run, run to recorded configuration and dataset, and code record to the existing commit. Each edge can fail independently, so preserve the missing or mismatched link instead of collapsing every result into a plausible name. The exact-generation download checks content against the lineage record, while local revision inspection checks whether the referenced code exists. Together they make provenance auditable from supplied records. They do not recover an absent lineage link by guesswork, even when deployment and experiment names look similar.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: Matching names are not matching lineage. A missing or mismatched run/artifact link must be reported, and an unverified revision string is not evidence that the code commit exists.
